title: Current-mirror OTA
description: A current-mirror (or current-amplifier) OTA: the input pair drives diode-connected mirror loads, and each mirror is copied with ratio $K_m$ to a push-out output branch, so the effective output transconductance is $K_m*g_{m,in}$. This buys bandwidth and slew almost for free — GBW = $K_m*g_{m,in}/(2*\pi*C_L)$ and SR = $K_m*I_{tail}/C_L$ — but not DC gain: raising $K_m$ scales both the output transconductance and the output conductance together, so the low-frequency gain is nearly independent of $K_m$. The catch shows up in noise: to hit a fixed GBW at larger $K_m$ the input pair shrinks ($g_{m,in}$ falls as $1/K_m$), so its input-referred thermal density grows as $\sqrt{K_m}$. Two mirror nodes carry poles: the PMOS node every branch passes (a full pole), and the bottom NMOS node only the folded branch passes (a pole-zero doublet). Both estimates are shown; settling is sim-owned.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. the budget carries about 30% headroom over the gamma-model row (no measured floor exists for this topology)

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the output mirror devices' vds

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.89-1.42 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. The max must stay below the diode-loaded drain (VDD minus the mirror's |vgs|) — both bracket ends have to size

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: K_m
params.note: mirror ratio: multiplies GBW and SR, but raises input noise as sqrt(K_m) at fixed GBW

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise floor

params.name: gm_id_ml
params.note: input-mirror (diode) inversion: sets the mirror-node pole

params.name: gm_id_mo
params.note: output-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher output resistance

doc.title: Input mirror device (diode)
doc.description: Diode-connected mirror load at half the tail current; its vds equals its own vgs and its gate node carries the mirror pole.

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, driving the diode mirror load. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain one diode drop below the supply, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the two.

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side)
doc.description: The K_m-scaled output copy carrying K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is one half of the output conductance and its gate cap loads the mirror node.

doc.title: Bottom mirror device (NMOS diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected NMOS that folds the second branch down to the bottom output device: one input branch reaches the output through its PMOS mirror alone, the other continues through this device to moutn. Carries the K_m-scaled current; its gate node is the second mirror pole. Diode-connected, so its drop is read off the vds = vgs diagonal.

doc.title: Output mirror device (NMOS side)
doc.description: The NMOS output copy sinking K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is the other half of the output conductance.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: Gm_out
rows.note: output transconductance = mirror ratio times the input gm

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output node loaded by both output mirror devices' conductance

rows.name: Av
rows.note: DC gain; K_m scales Gm_out and (via the K_m-larger output devices) Rout inversely, so gain is nearly K_m-independent

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the mirror load's own density referred by gm_mload/gm_in

rows.name: vn_gbw
rows.note: estimate: input density if the pair were sized to just meet GBW_target at this K_m — grows as sqrt(K_m), the current-mirror OTA's noise-for-bandwidth trade

rows.name: f_pole
rows.note: estimate: the PMOS mirror-node pole, set by the diode gm over its own plus the K_m-scaled output gate cap

rows.name: f_pole_n
rows.note: estimate: the bottom NMOS mirror-node pole, same accounting as f_pole on the folded branch

rows.name: PM
rows.note: estimate: the two mirror nodes cost phase differently, because the signal reaches them differently. BOTH input branches pass a PMOS mirror node, so $f_{pole}$ is a full pole in the whole path — unlike the 5T's mirror. Only the folded branch passes the bottom NMOS mirror, so half the signal is delayed there and $f_{pole,n}$ is a pole-ZERO DOUBLET (zero at twice the pole), costing far less phase. Measured against the ACHIEVED GBW, so overshooting the bandwidth target spends margin honestly

rules.note: estimate: margin left at crossover once the mirror node is paid for; advisory, since an open-loop OTA needs none of it and sim owns the real stability
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the diode load — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less diode drop
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges prove the range ENDS close, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, its own devices — and every hard rule must hold there

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way. Edges prove the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
